_comment: League payouts by season. Hand-maintained, and the one thing about the money
that cannot be fetched: MFL knows nothing about what the league pays out.
Source is the manager's meeting notes in Notion, one page per year. Every
season here is checked against a hard invariant before it is published: the
payouts must sum to exactly `teams x buyIn`. The league pays out the whole
pot, so a structure that does not reconcile is wrong, not approximate.
`stated` records what the notes actually say. Where a field is not stated it
is marked and the reconciliation is what justifies it -- see 2019/2020. A
season with no payout topic in its notes carried the previous year forward,
which is the league's own default and is also what reconciles.
2021 is the load-bearing year: the regular-season prize drops 195 -> 160 in
exactly the season the schedule goes 13 -> 14 weeks. 195 - 35 = 160, so the
extra weekly payout came straight out of it. That is corroboration, not
coincidence, and it is why the 2019/2020 champion figures can be trusted.
NOTHING BEFORE 2019. The league confirms the structure was genuinely
different then -- no weekly payouts at all, the regular-season prize came in
later, and the buy-in was raised at some point -- but those numbers are not
recorded anywhere available. The Yahoo era knows WHO won and cannot know
what they were paid, so it is left out rather than priced with the wrong
structure. Do not backfill it by assuming today's numbers.
A season is listed here BEFORE it is played so the weekly job has a
structure to price it with. An in-progress season is settled but never
reconciled -- only weekly money is decided until the Fantasy Bowl. The
reconciliation fires the moment season-end records the year, so an
assumption carried forward wrongly fails loudly instead of publishing.

seasons.note: Meeting notes state the weekly and regular-season figures; the regular-season prize was introduced this year. Champion and runner-up are the 2021 figures, which is what reconciles the pot to $1,000.
No payout topic in the 2020 notes, so 2019 carried forward. The notes cover only COVID contingencies, which did not trigger — the league confirms 2020 paid out normally.
Stated in full in the meeting notes.
No payout topic in the 2022 notes; 2021 carried forward.
No payout topic in the 2023 notes; carried forward.
No payout topic in the 2024 notes; carried forward.
Restructured for the 11-team league. The 2025 notes settle the $100 buy-in; the split is the one recorded in rules-data.js.

The 2026 meeting notes record a draft order but no resolutions at all, so 2025 carries forward — same 11 teams, same $100 buy-in. If the league did change something, the season will fail to reconcile at season-end rather than publish a wrong number; fix this row when it does.
